t.E124.agn: In its 2009 re-evaluation EFSA lowered the acceptable daily intake (ADI) for this colour and stated that intake in some adults and children may exceed the new limit. EFSA stated that the available data, including the Southampton study, did not confirm a causal link between individual colours and behavioural effects; the EU nevertheless kept the warning label mandatory for products containing it.
t.E124.body: In rats, mice and guinea pigs, almost all of the orally administered Ponceau 4R was excreted within 72 hours, most of it (about 90%) in faeces; no significant accumulation was seen in tissues. It is broken down in the gut contents; the main product in urine is naphthionic acid.
t.E124.eff.0.t: May have an adverse effect on activity and attention in children; in the EU this warning is mandatory on the label of products containing it. EFSA did not confirm a causal link with individual colours
t.E124.eff.1.t: The daily limit may be exceeded in some adults and children
t.E124.eval: In the EU, the labels of products containing this colour must carry the warning “may have an adverse effect on attention and activity in children” (following the 2007 Southampton study). In the US it is not permitted in food.
t.E124.prod: An azo dye produced by chemical synthesis.
t.E124.summary: A synthetic, red azo dye. It is used in confectionery, drinks and desserts.
